Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
244 PM EDT Mon Oct 26 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 243 PM EDT Monday...

No significant changes to the current forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 243 PM EDT Monday...

1. Behind a weak cold front this afternoon, high pressure will 
return with sharply colder air towards mid week. 

2. Light rain possible Thursday night as a frontal boundary 
moves through the region, then mostly dry and seasonably warm 
weather prevailing into the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 243 PM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: GOES-19 visible satellite depicts a narrow moisture 
corridor associated with a weak cold front stretched across the 
region this afternoon. While most of the radar returns have ended up 
being virga, some locations in the St. Lawrence Valley have been 
able to pick up a few hundreths of an inch of rainfall. By and large 
however, many locations will remain dry with little to no measurable 
rain from this frontal system, especially those in Vermont where 
dewpoint depressions are 10-15 degrees. A few places along the 
northwest facing slopes of the Adirondacks and northern Greens, 
including Jay Peak, could a few sprinkles though due to orographic 
influences. Winds will turn to the north-northwest as the front 
moves through this afternoon advecting sharply colder air and some 
briefly gusty winds this evening from Canada. As nocturnal cooling 
begins after sunset this evening, winds will briefly increase in the 
northern Champlain Valley up to 25 MPH or so between 7-10 PM. Winds 
will weaken towards calm thereafter. Tonights lows will cool to the 
upper 20s for many locations with a few locations hovering around 
the freezing mark in the wider valleys; coldest locations will be 
across northern New York and the Northeast Kingdom. Tomorrow will 
feature sunny skies with continued cool high temperatures struggling 
to reach the upper 40s. The coldest night of the season arrives 
Tuesday night under strong radiational cooling. Overnight lows may 
approach some records for Montpelier and St. Johnsbury, with records 
elsewhere residing in the 10th percentile or lower. Temperatures 
will drop to the teens across the Adirondacks and low 20s elsewhere. 
Temperatures slowly rebound Wednesday as high pressure and south 
winds help to moderate our pattern. Temperatures will warm to the 
low to mid 50s.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Low chances for some showers on Thursday night as a 
front crosses our area. With center of the low passing well north of 
our area, not a lot of strong forcing with this frontal passage. If 
we have precipitation, it will be light. Then we once again expect 
mostly dry and seasonably warm weather for Friday and Saturday as a 
ridge of surface high pressure builds into the north country. Some 
models indicate increasing chances for showers early next week, but 
not a lot of model consistency in that timeframe at this point. 
.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z MONDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Through 18Z Tuesday...Mainly VFR conditions today with exception
of brief MVFR ceilings as cold front drops across our area. Some
light rainfall has been observed as well. All terminals will 
trend back to VFR by 00z and are expected to remain that way for
the remainder of the forecast period. Winds tonight will 
generally be light and terrain influences, increasing out of the
south/southwest towards morning. Behind the front, winds shift 
to become more northwesterly and may be gusty at BTV and PBG 
with channeled flow. 

Outlook...

Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance
SHRA.
Friday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight chance SHRA.
Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.EQUIPMENT...
Routine observations from KSLK ASOS are unavailable until
further notice. While the site is operating, it is not able to
disseminate observations normally at this time. Technicians are
aware of the issue, but time of return to service is unknown.

&&
